name: Challow
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog cites only Ivani 2024 (languoid establishment, no title/details shown); no description of Challow stress located

sources.citation: CrossRef API queries 'Challow Trans-Himalayan Manipur' and 'Challow language' (saved query result).
sources.note: No other work on Challow indexed; only the Ivani 2024 Challow paper and its sibling Kongai field report (10.5070/h922259792) surface.

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2024 [eScholarship cover page dates it 2023; CrossRef issued 2023-08-20]. Some preliminary notes on Challow, a Trans-Himalayan language from Manipur, India. Himalayan Linguistics 22(2) (Languages and Peoples of the Eastern Himalayan Region): 1-12. DOI 10.5070/H922259698. CC BY-NC-ND.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 13-page PDF (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/pitch/prosody: zero hits). Section 2 'Phonological properties' gives the syllable template (C2)C1V(Cf)[T] (Figure 1, p.3), sesquisyllabic frozen prefixes with reduced centralized vowels (p.3, 2.4 pp.7-8), initials (2.2) and rhymes (2.3). Only prosodic remark, p.3: 'This study will not deal with tone; however, an impressionistic account of the data supported by comparative materials suggests that Challow has contrastive lexical tone (T) at the syllable level.' sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2023b. Challow 100-word Swadesh list (WAV audio, 100 files). Zenodo.
sources.note: The only primary data on the language; open citation-form audio could support a first-hand instrumental check of tone/prominence, but contains no descriptive statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page chal1279 (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), and hh.bib record vw:Ivani:Challow (glottolog_ref_id 679501, listed by Glottolog as a comparative study;wordlist).
sources.note: No stress content. Confirms Ivani 2024 is the sole reference: 'Challow.. is first mentioned in Jessica K. Ivani 2024. It is not intelligible to neighbouring languages and thus constitutes a separate (probably Tangkhulic) language.' AES status threatened.

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. (any future work on Challow / the minor languages of Ukhrul district, University of Zurich) - nothing found in CrossRef or Zenodo as of 2026-09-17.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2024 paper explicitly defers tone and all further prosody to future study; a follow-up by the same author would be the first source that could contain a stress or tone statement.
